title: Personal Information Disclosure During Registration
description: During account registration, the homeowner provides personally identifiable information (PII) such as name, address, and contact details. This information could be intercepted, misused, or exposed to unauthorized parties, leading to identity theft or privacy violations.

title: Camera/Sensor Data Disclosure
description: Enrolling cameras and sensors on the Home Hub may capture sensitive visual and audio data of the homeowner's private activities, including daily routines, conversations, and potentially sensitive events. This data could be accessed by unauthorized parties or leaked through system vulnerabilities.

title: Activity Linkability Across Systems
description: Data collected from the Home Hub could potentially be linked to the homeowner's activities across other platforms or services, creating a comprehensive profile of the homeowner's behavior, location patterns, and lifestyle.

title: Account Takeover During Registration
description: During the account registration process, there is a risk of credential stuffing, phishing, or social engineering attacks that could allow an attacker to impersonate the homeowner and gain unauthorized access to the Home Hub system.

title: Guest access linked to identity
description: The Home Hub may log guest access codes and link them to guest identity, enabling correlation of access events with personal information

title: Access code disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The temporary access code may be visible to others, logged insecurely, or transmitted without encryption, allowing unauthorized disclosure

title: Unauthorized use of access code
description: If the temporary access code is shared or compromised, an unauthorized person could gain access to the home

title: Guest identifiable through access patterns
description: Access logs may reveal guest identity through timing, frequency, or location of access code entry

title: Guest cannot prove non-entry
description: Guest may be unable to prove they did not enter the access code if challenged, due to lack of authentication evidence

title: Privacy Disclosure through Motion/Door/Sensor Events
description: Motion, door, and sensor events written to the local event log may reveal patterns of life, presence at home, daily routines, and occupancy patterns, potentially disclosing sensitive personal information about household members.
assumptions: Event log is accessible to unauthorized parties or could be exfiltrated

title: Linkability of Events to Individuals
description: Sensor events may be linkable to specific individuals or activities, enabling correlation of different events to build a comprehensive profile of household behavior and routines.
assumptions: Events contain sufficient context to link to specific individuals

title: Event Log Tampering and Integrity Compromise
description: The local event log could be tampered with, modified, or deleted by unauthorized actors, compromising the integrity of the recorded events and potentially enabling denial of activities.
assumptions: Event log is not adequately protected from unauthorized modification

title: Identification of Individuals from Event Metadata
description: Metadata associated with events (timestamps, locations, device IDs) could potentially be used to identify specific individuals or their presence in specific areas.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about whether events contain explicit identifying information

title: Video data leakage during upload
description: Video clips may be intercepted during transmission from Home Hub to Cloud Storage via unencrypted or compromised network channels

title: Home Hub impersonation
description: Malicious actors may impersonate the Home Hub to upload unauthorized or malicious video data to Cloud Storage

title: Unauthorized access to stored video footage
description: Cloud video storage may be vulnerable to unauthorized access, allowing third parties to view private surveillance footage

title: Video footage tampering
description: Stored video data may be altered, deleted, or manipulated by unauthorized parties, compromising evidence integrity

title: Video footage reveals identifiable individuals
description: Surveillance video may capture faces, license plates, or other personally identifiable information of individuals in the monitored area

title: Video data can be linked to specific individuals or events
description: Video footage may be correlated with other data sources (e.g., timestamps, metadata) to identify individuals or track movements across time

title: Privacy regulation violations
description: Video storage and processing may not comply with GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations regarding consent, data retention, and user rights

title: Linkability of Motion Alerts Across Time
description: Motion alerts forwarded from the Home Hub can be linked to specific users or locations over time, enabling the creation of movement profiles that reveal patterns of occupancy and behavior.
assumptions: The system retains historical motion alert data and associates it with user accounts or device identifiers.

title: Inference of User Presence from Motion Data
description: Real-time motion alerts can reveal when individuals are present or absent from the home, potentially identifying specific users based on movement patterns and timing.
assumptions: Motion detection is sensitive enough to distinguish between different occupants or infer presence/absence.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Motion Alert Data
description: Motion alert data transmitted to the Mobile App Backend could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the backend is compromised or if data is accessed without proper authorization.
assumptions: The backend has access controls that may be insufficient or vulnerable to exploitation.

title: Usurpation of Home Hub Identity
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the Home Hub to send false motion alerts or intercept legitimate alerts, compromising the integrity of the privacy system.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms between the Home Hub and backend are weak or absent.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of motion detection data
description: Motion-detected notification could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties, revealing when and where motion was detected at the homeowner's property.

title: Linkability of motion data to other personal information
description: Motion detection notifications could be linked with other data about the homeowner's activities, location patterns, or presence at home, creating a comprehensive profile.

title: Identification of homeowner from notification metadata
description: Notification metadata (timing, frequency, device identifiers) could potentially be used to identify the specific homeowner or infer their habits and routines.

title: Usurpation of notification delivery
description: An attacker could potentially intercept or redirect notifications to the homeowner's device, or impersonate the homeowner to receive notifications meant for them.

title: Linkability of Aggregated Analytics
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics shared with the cloud analytics vendor may be linkable to specific users or devices through cross-referencing with other data sources, potentially enabling re-identification.
assumptions: The cloud analytics vendor has access to additional data sources that could be correlated with the shared analytics.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure to Third Parties
description: The cloud analytics vendor may share or sell the aggregated device-usage analytics to third parties without proper authorization or user consent, violating privacy expectations.
assumptions: The vendor's privacy policy and data sharing agreements are not sufficiently restrictive or are not enforced.

title: Inference of User Behavior Patterns
description: Even aggregated analytics may reveal sensitive behavioral patterns or preferences about user groups, enabling inference of information beyond what was explicitly shared.
assumptions: The aggregation level is insufficient to prevent pattern recognition or statistical inference attacks.

title: Data Integrity Compromise
description: The cloud analytics vendor may alter, corrupt, or tamper with the aggregated device-usage analytics during storage or processing, compromising data integrity.
assumptions: The vendor's security controls and data handling procedures are inadequate.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: The cloud analytics vendor may process the shared analytics in violation of applicable privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding data transfer, storage, or usage.
assumptions: The vendor operates in multiple jurisdictions with varying privacy requirements and may not maintain adequate compliance documentation.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Video Content During Transmission
description: Video clip data transmitted from cloud storage to mobile app backend could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Transmission channel is not fully encrypted or authentication is weak

title: Video Content Tampering During Transmission
description: Video clip data could be modified or corrupted during transmission from cloud storage to mobile app backend, compromising data integrity.
assumptions: Transmission channel lacks integrity verification mechanisms

title: Video Content Reveals Homeowner Identity and Location
description: Video content retrieved by mobile app backend could reveal the identity, location, or activities of the homeowner, leading to identification risks.
assumptions: Video contains identifiable visual information about the homeowner or their property

title: Video Data Linked to Other Personal Information
description: Video clip data could be linked to other personal data about the homeowner (e.g., name, address, contact info) through metadata or cross-referencing, increasing identifiability.
assumptions: Video metadata or associated data contains linking information

title: Unauthorized Access to Video Playback
description: Mobile app backend could be accessed by unauthorized users who impersonate the homeowner, allowing them to view video content they should not access.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are weak or compromised
